title: 🔒 Security: SSRF via DNS Resolution Bypass in web-fetch Tool (CVSS 8.6)

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable security bug report regarding SSRF via DNS resolution bypass in the web-fetch tool, with detailed explanation of the root cause, affected code locations, and impact.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is localized to `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts`, updating `isBlockedHost` to call the existing async `isPrivateIpAsync` utility function and updating its internal callers to await the result.

summary.problem: The web-fetch tool uses synchronous IP address validation without DNS resolution, enabling SSRF attacks via domains resolving to private IP addresses.
summary.root_cause: isBlockedHost in packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts calls isPrivateIp(), which only checks literal IP address strings and returns false for domain names.
summary.context: packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ts already contains isPrivateIpAsync() which resolves hostnames via DNS lookup before checking for private IP addresses.

steps: Import isPrivateIpAsync instead of isPrivateIp from ../utils/fetch.js in packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts.
Refactor isBlockedHost in WebFetchToolInvocation to be an async method that calls and awaits isPrivateIpAsync(urlStr).
Update callers of isBlockedHost in packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts (executeFallbackForUrl, filterAndValidateUrls, executeExperimental, and getConfirmationDetails) to await isBlockedHost.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: Web fetch requests targeting domain names that resolve to private IP addresses are blocked appropriately.
verification_steps: Update existing unit tests and add tests in packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.test.ts to verify that domain names resolving to private IP addresses are blocked by isBlockedHost.
